newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKS TAKE GAME 3 FROM ORIOLES ON EIGHTH-INNING RALLY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKS TAKE GAME 3 FROM ORIOLES ON EIGHTH-INNING RALLY.

text.p: The New York Yankees erupted for four runs in a two-out, eighth-inning rally to beat the Orioles 5-2 on Friday and grab a two games to one lead in the American League Championship Series.
Yankees starter Jimmy Key turned in a brilliant performance from the mound. He gave up a first-inning two-run homer to Todd Zeile and little else in shutting down the powerful Baltimore lineup.
"Todd hit a pitch that I didn't think was that bad of a pitch. He hit it out of the park and I said 'well forget about that and go from here,'" Key said of his one errant toss.

Key allowed just three hits in eight innings -- none after the second -- with one walk and five strikeouts. He retired 23 of the last 26 batters he faced to improve to 4-1 in seven career post-season games.
New York's star closer John Wetteland finished up with a perfect ninth for the save.
Key had been locked in a classic pitchers' deul with Baltimore starter Mike Mussina through the first seven innings.
Mussina had scattered four hits and allowed just one run over the first seven innings. But he ended up being charged with five runs and eight hits over 7 2/3 innings.
The Yankees were trailing 2-1 in the eighth and down to their last four outs when rookie sensation Derek Jeter ripped a double into the right field corner to start the big rally.

Bernie Williams followed with a single to left that brought Jeter dashing home with the tying run. The Yankees had been a frustrated 2-for-27 in the series with runners in scoring position before Williams' single.
Mussina, who had been practically untouchable early, then surrendered a double to Tino Martinez that sent Williams safely to third.

That's when Zeile went from hero to goat. The Orioles third baseman took the throw from left fielder B.J. Surhoff and tried to fake a throw to second. But the ball slipped out of his hand, bouncing away. With that, Willams raced home, sliding safely over the plate with the go-ahead run.
Cecil Fielder followed with the fourth consecutive Yankee hit -- a towering two-run homer that put New York up 5-2 and sent Mussina to the showers.
"Mike's a great pitcher, especially here in this ballpark," Key said of Mussina. "I had to keep it close because he's not going to make many mistakes and it took 'til the eighth inning to do it.
"Our guys didn't give up, they kept battling and finally we got to him," Key said.
With their fifth come-from-behind victory of these playoffs, the Yankees raised their perfect record at Camden Yards this year to 7-0 after winning all six regular-season meetings in Baltimore.
Game 4 in the best-of-seven series is set for Saturday in Baltimore.
The National League Championship series also resumes Saturday in St Louis with the defending World Series champion Atlanta Braves and the Cardinals tied at one game each.
